def: NumPy's n-dimensional array: a flat block of memory plus a header giving dtype, shape, strides and offset.
The data type of an array's elements, such as float32 or int64, which fixes bytes per element and the arithmetic used.
The tuple giving the number of elements along each axis of an array, written (rows, columns) for a matrix.
The number of bytes to step in memory to move one position along each axis of an array.
A memory layout in which the last axis varies fastest, so each row of a matrix is contiguous; also called C order.
An array that describes the same memory as another array, so writing through one changes the other.
An array with its own newly allocated memory, independent of the array it was made from.
An operation such as sum, mean or max that collapses one or more axes of an array into single values.
The rule that lets arrays of different shapes combine by aligning shapes from the right and stretching axes of size 1.
NumPy's Einstein-summation function, which writes a tensor product by naming each axis with a letter and listing which letters survive.
The rules that decide the dtype of a result when operands have different dtypes.
An array whose elements sit next to each other in memory in the order the layout implies, so reads stream efficiently.
